extracted.intended_audience: Coast Guard contract administrators, contracting officers, COTRs, auditors and policy makers involved in A-76/commercial activity procurements
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate performance, cost-effectiveness, and administration of Coast Guard A-76 service contracts by comparing contract costs to MEO/MEO personnel costs, reviewing contract files and modifications, and assessing QA, staffing, wage adjustments, and contractor stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to Government's MEO (Most Efficient Organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare actual contract cost with the Government's MEO (should-cost) to determine whether the activity is operating at a savings to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEG/MEO costs were computed using instructions from the OMB Circular, including current standard Government GS and Military pay scales with annual inflation and retirement factors provided by OMB. Use the MEO (should cost) as a benchmark; recompute the MEO when scope changes or when original conditions no longer apply. Examples: Tables XV–XVIII show percent differences between contract costs and MEO personnel cost. Note that MEG costs are not maintained by MLCPAC and may require retrieval from COMDT (G-CPP-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial award savings threshold (10% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts were initially awarded only when the contractor's bid was lower than the Government's MEO by 10% or greater of MEG personnel cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the contractor bid is less than the MEO by less than 10% (e.g., 5.4%), the contract award should be questioned. The report notes cases where initial contracts were less than the required 10% and likely should not have been awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of OMB Circular A-76 cost-comparison guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconstruct cost comparisons following OMB Circular A-76 guidelines when evaluating whether contracts produce savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow A-76 procedures (use proper pay scales, inflation/retirement factors) to compute MEO and compare to contract costs; the report uses this method to conclude some contracts should not have been awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and timeliness of wage determinations and economic price adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply DOL wage determinations and economic price adjustments accurately and in a timely manner; these adjustments materially affect contract costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: DOL Wage Determination 85-1158 and 86-413 were applied; economic price adjustment for food (1.15%) and combined wage/food adjustments produced sizable mods (e.g., $30,407). An inaccurate or low wage determination used at solicitation can lead to underestimating future costs and erode savings (Support Center Alameda example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation completeness in contract files
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract files should be complete and able to stand on their own for later review; missing documentation impedes reconstructing why actions were taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report found transferred files from D17 to MLCPAC were incomplete; some actions taken by MLCPAC could not be explained by documentation or recollection. Complete post-negotiation memoranda, obligations, deobligations and mods should be recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of contract award / avoidance of excessive extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitation, negotiation and award should occur promptly so contracts are in place at the end of prior option periods; excessive extensions indicate process delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed delays: awards issued 1.5 months to one year after the end of the contract's final option year. Causes include slow specification review/approval, long DCAA audit lead times, heavy contract specialist workload, and long negotiation prep time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and adequacy of Contractor QA Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor must provide a Quality Assurance (QA) Plan to enable monitoring of contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lack of a contractor QA Plan was identified as a major problem (Support Center Alameda). The Contract Specialist had to request the overdue QA plan; absence makes it difficult to justify deductions for unsatisfactory performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and adequacy of Government QA surveillance plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Government (COTR/contracting office) must have an implemented QA surveillance plan to monitor contractor performance and support performance-based deductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COTR expressed that QA paperwork requirements were a gray area and that MLCPAC Contract Specialist was too busy to assist in developing surveillance plans. Without a QA surveillance plan it is difficult to properly justify deduction amounts for unsatisfactory performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTR training and applicability to day-to-day duties
rubrics_metrics.description: COTRs should receive training that adequately addresses their day-to-day duties, QA methods, and lessons learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although many COTRs attended COTR/QA courses that provided basic contracting fundamentals, the report notes courses did not adequately cover day-to-day COTR duties or lessons learned and that methods to ensure QA were vague. COTR tenure varied (3 months to 4 years) and experience levels differed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor personnel qualifications and turnover
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor must provide fully qualified personnel as required by contract specifications; excessive turnover and hiring unqualified workers are deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support Center Alameda experienced high turnover and new employees hired 'off the street' who were not fully qualified, violating contract specifications. Wage rates that are too low can hamper recruitment/retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor project manager (PM) leadership and supervisory capability
rubrics_metrics.description: PM must demonstrate leadership and supervisory skills appropriate to the contract; poor PM leadership/communication contributes to marginal performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: PM operating at a working level rather than supervisory role led to marginal performance; conversely, motivated prior-service PMs who understand military customers improved food service contract outcomes (e.g., Mr. Griffin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and tracking of contract modifications and reasons (e.g., continuing resolutions, claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: All contract modifications (amounts, dates, reasons) must be tracked and explained in the contract file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many mods were due to Congressional continuing resolutions, wage determinations, economic price adjustments, claims for damage, or deobligations. Tables XI–XIV summarize mods; modifications affected total obligated amounts vs contract price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of deobligations for reductions in usage (e.g., meals sold)
rubrics_metrics.description: When actual activity (e.g., meals sold) is below estimates, deobligations should be applied to offset contract costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Food service contracts experienced deobligations when meals sold were below estimates, which offset cost increases. Examples: deobligation credits and estimated deobligations reduced actual contract price below original estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and adjusting MEO for scope changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recompute and adjust the MEO when the scope of the contract changes to ensure the 'should-cost' remains accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support Center Seattle's MEO did not reflect current contract conditions after a reduction in scope; the report recommends recomputing MEO when significant scope or service coverage changes occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of original contract award cost as funding base with active monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Original negotiated contract price is used as the basis for Headquarters funding, but funding bases must be monitored and adjusted as contract costs change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report notes funding bases have not been changed after initial funding despite cost increases or decreases; contract overruns are 'covered' within budgets rather than prompting review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of contractor financial stability and default risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and consider contractor financial condition as part of contract risk evaluation, since default could leave insufficient Government personnel to perform the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanding Officer expressed concern about contractor financial condition and the lack of available Coast Guard SSs in Alaska to substitute if contractor defaults. Contractor under new ownership considered more stable than before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification clarity and degree of allowable flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract specifications should be sufficiently detailed to limit excessive contractor flexibility that could affect costs or performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad specifications allowed contractors flexibility to provide extras (e.g., selling food at cost for morale events) which were possible due to good profit margins; overly broad specs can mask actual responsibilities and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification and documentation for deductions for unsatisfactory performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Deductions taken for unsatisfactory performance must be supported by QA surveillance documentation to be properly justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deductions were taken for incidents (sleeping on patrol, missed rounds and falsified logs) but, without QA surveillance plans, it was difficult to justify the amount of these deductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of projected cost growth in award decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating whether to award or renew a contract, consider projected cost growth (e.g., from wage increases) relative to projected MEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The second Ketchikan contract showed projected contract cost growth led to being 41.4% over projected MEO; such projections should prompt further analysis before award/renewal. For Support Center Alameda, projected wage increases could cause contract costs to exceed MEO personnel costs by up to 14% in later option years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of wage rates on recruitment and contract performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure offered wage rates are competitive in the local market; low wages lead to staffing problems and marginal performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support Center Alameda's initial wage rate was lower than other local security contracts, making it difficult to attract qualified employees and increasing turnover; subsequent wage increases improved workforce stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of experienced prior-service PMs to smooth contractor transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining the same, motivated prior-service PM across contractor changeover improves contract continuity and success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: retaining Mr. Griffin (prior-service SS) as Head Cook during contractor changeover greatly improved operations; motivated prior-service PMs were a big factor in successful food service contracts.
